1.explanation: These two files implement the ‘external‐anchors‐use‐rel‐noopener’ audit. The gatherer (anchors-with-no-rel-noopener.js) selects all <a> elements with target="_blank" but no rel="noopener", and the audit (external-anchors-use-rel-noopener.js) reports them. Neither currently filters out mailto: links. To fix, they both need logic to skip URLs whose href starts with “mailto:”, so those links aren’t audited or flagged.
1.bug_scenario: The “external-anchors-use-rel-noopener” audit is flagging mailto: links (with target="_blank") as missing rel="noopener". When users follow the audit suggestion and add rel="noopener" to mailto: links, the links break on Chrome for Android and iOS Safari (they no longer open the mail client). The audit should ignore mailto: URLs entirely.

2.explanation: The gatherer anchors-with-no-rel-noopener.js collects all <a> elements missing rel=noopener, regardless of protocol. The audit external-anchors-use-rel-noopener.js then flags every non-same-origin link—including mailto:. Because adding rel=noopener breaks mailto: on mobile, both the gatherer (to filter out mailto:) and the audit (to ignore mailto:) must be updated. These two files drive the detection logic and therefore need patching.
2.bug_scenario: The “External anchors use rel=noopener” audit is flagging mailto: links (e.g. <a href="mailto:support@…" rel="noopener">) as requiring rel=noopener. When we apply rel=noopener to a mailto: link, Chrome on Android and Safari on iOS fail to open the native mail client. The audit report shows both sales@ and support@ links but only the support@ link had rel=noopener applied—and that one now fails to launch mail. We need to ignore mailto: URIs in this audit.
